analysis.title: The FOMC Was Predictably Boring
key_insights: The FOMC held the fed funds target range at 3.75%-4% on Oct 28, 2026, as widely expected and priced. Markets barely moved in Treasury yields, the USD and equities.
OIS pricing for the December 9 meeting was trimmed by 1-2bps but still leans heavily toward a hike, which Scotiabank expects.

Scotiabank's view is that the main argument for skipping a hike was that a surprise hike would violate the dots. It would have created urgency in markets and pushed them to price another move in December.
The vote was 10-2. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a 25bp hike. Kashkari and Logan, two of the previously most hawkish members, did not dissent this time.

The statement changed little. It now says the accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the appropriate policy stance. It upgraded economic activity to a 'strong' pace from 'solid'.
Chair Warsh stressed the strength of the US economy and growth and labour markets, said the full focus remains on inflation, and noted that financial conditions have tightened.

The Fed will reduce decision meetings. The eight-meeting schedule is kept in 2027, but one meeting will be a strategy meeting with no statement or policy vote. In 2028 there will be six decision meetings and two strategy meetings.
Balance sheet plans: the balance sheet task force's conclusions will go to the FOMC probably early in Q1 2027. Warsh declined to commit to the timing.

Five task forces (communications, balance sheet, data sources, productivity and jobs, inflation frameworks) are working toward a year-end deadline. Some but not all will meet it. The productivity and jobs task force holds a field hearing on Nov 16.

Warsh declined to say whether the Committee has broad support for another hike this year, saying he does not believe in forward guidance in normal times. Members can speak once the blackout period ends.

On oil, Warsh said the historically strong correlation between oil prices and interest rates has weakened recently. Energy prices have risen while rates have fallen, and futures prices have moved up over recent weeks.

On AI, Warsh said rates have affected both tech and non-tech investment since September, spreads have widened, and the capex story is broadening. He said he does not see economic growth as causing inflation.
Scotiabank notes Warsh looks backward in his assessments while BoC Governor Macklem is forecast-focused.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Unchanged after the 25bp hike on Sept 16. Markets saw the communications as slightly dovish.
Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike. Fewer hawkish dissents than expected reduces pressure for an immediate move.

macro_indicators.reading: hike expected by Scotiabank and leaned toward by OIS
macro_indicators.interpretation: OIS pricing was trimmed by 1-2bps but still leans heavily toward a hike.
Warsh said there is no soft inflation target and that it is a 2% target measured by PCE.

risk_factors: A surprise hike would have created urgency in markets and pricing of further moves, adding internal tension on the FOMC.
Awkward communications at the December meeting, just before the most hawkish voting members lose their votes in the new year.
Warsh said inflation remains elevated and focused on inflation, with no progress toward the 2% target per the press conference question.
Energy prices have risen and futures prices have moved up over the last several weeks.
vol_and_positioning: Markets barely reacted across Treasury yields, the USD and equities. OIS for December 9 was trimmed by 1-2bps.
geopolitical: The FOMC statement cites geopolitical developments as one source of elevated uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: Scotiabank expects a December 9 hike. OIS still leans heavily toward one, inflation remains elevated per the statement, and Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Kashkari and Logan stopped dissenting, Warsh declined to endorse further hikes or forward guidance, and he said the medicine is starting to work. Tighter financial conditions and falling rates could reduce the need to hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Warsh said the period in front of the Fed is information rich. Data and Committee speeches after the blackout period ends will decide the December outcome.

theme_stances.key_argument: A surprise hike in October would have violated the dots and added tension, so the Fed waited, and Scotiabank expects a hike on December 9.
Warsh announced fewer decision meetings from 2027-28, with strategy meetings carrying no statement or vote.
theme_stances.evidence: the number of meetings at which policy decisions would be delivered would be reduced
